ELCT 101.description: Introductions to: the profession of electrical engineering; the wide range of sub-disciplines that make electrical engineering so valuable in improving the human condition; the role of electrical engineers in society; and the role of electrical engineering students in the university.
ELCT 101.subject: ELCT
ELCT 101.title: Electrical and Electronics Engineering

ELCT 102.description: Fundamentals of electrical and electronic components. Basic network laws. Mathematical and computer tools for network analysis.
ELCT 102.subject: ELCT
ELCT 102.title: Electrical Science

ELCT 201.description: Laboratory procedures, instrumentation and measurements, report writing, computer use in system design, testing, and troubleshooting. Integrative project-based learning environment including passive, active, electronic and electromechanical systems.
ELCT 201.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENGL 102 and C or better in CSCE 211.
ELCT 201.subject: ELCT
ELCT 201.title: Introductory Electrical Engineering Laboratory

ELCT 220.description: Fundamentals of electrical engineering for mechanical, chemical, or other engineering disciplines, including electric circuits, measurements, data acquisition, sensors, motors, and controllers.
ELCT 220.subject: ELCT
ELCT 220.title: Electrical Engineering for Non-Majors

ELCT 221.description: Analysis of linear ac circuits using complex variables. Nodal and mesh analysis, Thevenin and Norton transformations, linearity, superposition, use of math solvers, circuit simulators, and computer-interfaced instrumentation.
ELCT 221.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 142; C or better in either ELCT 102 or AESP 265 or D or better in ELCT 220.
ELCT 221.subject: ELCT
ELCT 221.title: Circuits

ELCT 222.description: Analysis of continuous-time signals and systems in time and frequency domains, Fourier series and transforms, Laplace transforms; introduction to discrete-time signals.
ELCT 222.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 221 and in MATH 242.
ELCT 222.subject: ELCT
ELCT 222.title: Signals and Systems

ELCT 301.description: Design and implementation of analog and digital electronic circuits, with emphasis on developing deep individual understanding of curriculum-spanning concepts.
ELCT 301.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 201.
ELCT 301.subject: ELCT
ELCT 301.title: Electronics Laboratory

ELCT 302.description: Team-oriented application of sensing, measurement, and real time embedded digital control for autonomous vehicular systems. Requirements analysis, system modeling, software/hardware integration, report writing, development of teaming skills.
ELCT 302.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 301 and ELCT 371.
ELCT 302.subject: ELCT
ELCT 302.title: Real Time Systems Laboratory

ELCT 321.description: An introduction to analysis, design and applications of discrete time systems; z- and discrete Fourier transforms; frequency and impulse responses, FIR and IIR filters.
ELCT 321.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 222.
ELCT 321.subject: ELCT
ELCT 321.title: Digital Signal Processing

ELCT 331.description: Fundamentals of control systems. Analysis and design of control systems using physical system models. State variables, steady-state error, time- and frequency-responses, control system stability. Root locus analysis and controller design – PI, PD, PID, lead-lag compensator. Nyquist stability criterion.
ELCT 331.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 222.
ELCT 331.subject: ELCT
ELCT 331.title: Control Systems

ELCT 350.description: Formulation of physics-based dynamic models of electrical or electromechanical systems. Solving dynamic equations of electrical systems in discrete time. Use of object oriented programming language (e.g., C++) and computer tools (e.g, MATLAB, virtual test bed) for solving dynamic equations of electrical systems.
ELCT 350.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 222, C or better in CSCE 145.
ELCT 350.subject: ELCT
ELCT 350.title: Computer Modeling of Electrical Systems

ELCT 361.description: Basic concepts of electric and magnetic fields, including electrostatics, magnetostatics, and quasi-statics with computer applications.
ELCT 361.subject: ELCT
ELCT 361.title: Electromagnetics

ELCT 363.description: Properties and characteristics of semiconductor materials, p-n and semiconductor-metal junctions. Basic properties, characteristics and operation of diodes and transistors.
ELCT 363.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHEM 111 and PHYS 212.
ELCT 363.subject: ELCT
ELCT 363.title: Introduction to Microelectronics

ELCT 371.description: Introduction to design and analysis of electronic circuits and systems. Applications of amplifiers, op-amps, diodes, bipolar and field-effect transistors in analog and digital circuits.
ELCT 371.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 222.
ELCT 371.subject: ELCT
ELCT 371.title: Electronics

ELCT 391.description: Fundamentals of non-invasive probes for biometrics. Principles of ultrasound for echocardiography, optoelectronics for photoplethysmography, and electrochemistry for electrocardiography and electroencephalography. Introduction to amplification methods for biometric probe readout electronics. Studies of engineering tradeoffs between signal level versus adverse effects. Measurement basics of signals.
ELCT 391.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 141 or MATH 122; D or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
ELCT 391.subject: ELCT
ELCT 391.title: Biometric Measurements in Healthcare and Wearables

ELCT 403.description: Planning, preliminary design, and prototyping. Analysis and specification of system and subsystem requirements, measures of performance, analysis of alternatives, effective team work. Project management and scheduling. Prototype implementation and characterization. This course should be taken during student’s penultimate semester.
ELCT 403.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 302.
ELCT 403.subject: ELCT
ELCT 403.title: Capstone Design Project I

ELCT 404.description: Continuation of Capstone Design Project I. Final design and implementation including design iteration, design for reliability, system integration and characterization, business case development.
ELCT 404.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 403.
ELCT 404.subject: ELCT
ELCT 404.title: Capstone Design Project II

ELCT 432.description: Introduction to communication systems, sampling theorem, modulation theory, multiplexing, phase-lock loops, and related topics.
ELCT 432.subject: ELCT
ELCT 432.title: Fundamentals of Communication Systems

ELCT 499.description: Individual investigation or studies of special topics. A maximum of 3 credits total may be applied toward a degree. Advanced approval of project proposal by instructor and department advisor.
ELCT 499.subject: ELCT
ELCT 499.title: Special Problems

ELCT 510.description: Fundamentals of photovoltaic solar cell technologies. Design and operation of solar cells, including efficiency analysis and cost benefit. Applications to green and sustainable energy systems.
ELCT 510.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 363.
ELCT 510.subject: ELCT
ELCT 510.title: Photovoltaic Materials and Devices

ELCT 521.description: Introduction to plane electromagnetic wave propagation, reflection, transmission, antennas and antenna arrays, wireless link margin; noise, noise figure, noise temperature; switches and phase shifters; microwave modeling.
ELCT 521.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 361 or PHYS 504.
ELCT 521.subject: ELCT
ELCT 521.title: Introduction to Microwave Engineering

ELCT 530.description: The embedded electronics and software used in data acquisition, and process and instrument control in an industrial or manufacturing environment.
ELCT 530.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 331, or departmental approval.
ELCT 530.subject: ELCT
ELCT 530.title: Industrial Controls

ELCT 531.description: Analysis and design of discrete-time control systems, implementation of control systems using digital electronic systems. Applications to electrical systems.
ELCT 531.subject: ELCT
ELCT 531.title: Digital Control Systems

ELCT 533.description: Sensing, data acquisition, and data processing for evaluation of performance and system health. Integration and implementation of health management systems.
ELCT 533.subject: ELCT
ELCT 533.title: System Health Management

ELCT 541.description: Operating principles and design of bioelectric sensors and sensor systems for medical applications.
ELCT 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 361, ELCT 363 and ELCT 371.
ELCT 541.subject: ELCT
ELCT 541.title: Sensors for Biomedicine

ELCT 551.description: Electric power systems including transformer fundamentals, per-unit analysis, transmission and distribution line design, power flow analysis, optimal power flow and power system simulations.
ELCT 551.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ELCT 221, or departmental approval.
ELCT 551.subject: ELCT
ELCT 551.title: Power Systems Design and Analysis

ELCT 553.description: Analysis and design of electromechanical energy conversion systems, including electrical machines and electronic drives.
ELCT 553.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 331, ELCT 361 and ELCT 451.
ELCT 553.subject: ELCT
ELCT 553.title: Electromechanical Energy Conversion

ELCT 554.description: Analysis and design of power systems in presence of photovoltaic generation with focus on protection systems, control, power quality.
ELCT 554.subject: ELCT
ELCT 554.title: Integration of Photovoltaics in Modern Power Systems

ELCT 559.description: Special topics in distributed energy resources for modern electrical energy systems. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. May be repeated as topics vary.
ELCT 559.subject: ELCT
ELCT 559.title: Special Topics in Distributed Energy Resources for Electric Energy Systems

ELCT 562.description: Fourier techniques and stochastic processes review, multiple access cellular techniques, signal space representations for signals and noise, baseband modulations and optimal receivers in additive white Gaussian noise, bandpass and higher-order modulations, mobile wireless propagation channel characteristics, effects of bandlimiting distortion mitigation, diversity techniques.
ELCT 562.subject: ELCT
ELCT 562.title: Wireless Communications

ELCT 563.description: Operational principles and characteristics of electronic and optoelectronic semiconductor devices including MOSFETs and high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) for power electronics, electric cars and high-speed communications, light emitting diodes and lasers for solid state lighting, displays and optical communication, solar cells for green power generation.
ELCT 563.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 363.
ELCT 563.subject: ELCT
ELCT 563.title: Semiconductor Devices for Power, Communications and Lighting

ELCT 564.description: RF design fundamentals, lumped elements, transmission line theory, transmission lines and waveguides, S-parameters, impedance matching, microwave resonators.
ELCT 564.subject: ELCT
ELCT 564.title: RF Circuit Design for Wireless Communications

ELCT 572.description: Basic analysis and design of solid-state power electronic devices and circuitry.
ELCT 572.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ELCT 371.
ELCT 572.subject: ELCT
ELCT 572.title: Power Electronics

ELCT 574.description: Semiconductor material and device characterization; resistivity, carrier and doping density, contact resistance, Schottky barriers, series resistance, defects, trapped charges, and carrier lifetime.
ELCT 574.subject: ELCT
ELCT 574.title: Semiconductor Materials and Device Characterization

ELCT 732.description: Plane wave propagation and effects of various media. Distinct propagation mechanism descriptions. Mathematics for computing field strengths and powers for different propagation mechanisms. Antenna/noise principles. Wireless channel effects on signaling. Channel modeling as linear, time-varying filter. Delay/Doppler spreads. Empirical statistical wireless channel models. Multi-antenna channel characteristics.
ELCT 732.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ELCT 562 or successful completion of undergraduate courses in electromagnetics, probability/statistics, and linear system theory.
ELCT 732.subject: ELCT
ELCT 732.title: Radio Propagation Wireless Channel Modeling

ELCT 751.description: Network analysis methods suitable for computer implementation. System studies, including load-flow analysis, short-circuit analysis, and state estimation.
ELCT 751.subject: ELCT
ELCT 751.title: Advanced Power Systems Analysis

ELCT 753.description: Dynamics of electrical machine and space phasor theory. Analysis and design of control architecture for electrical motors.
ELCT 753.subject: ELCT
ELCT 753.title: Electrical Drives

ELCT 761.description: Theorems and principles of EM theory, Maxwell's equations, vector and scalar potentials. Solution to Maxwell's equation in one-, two-, and three-dimensions. Green's functions and theorems with applications to radiation and guided-wave propagation.
ELCT 761.subject: ELCT
ELCT 761.title: Fundamental Electromagnetics

ELCT 762.description: The concept of signal integrity for high speed circuits, signal parameters, transmission lines, I/O buffer models, clock schemes, serial data, package/die/connector modeling, I/O power delivery, and measurement.
ELCT 762.subject: ELCT
ELCT 762.title: Signal Integrity for High Speed Circuits

ELCT 763.description: Computer-aided semiconductor device modeling and simulation; Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) tools for modern semiconductor devices.
ELCT 763.subject: ELCT
ELCT 763.title: Semiconductor Device Modeling and Simulation

ELCT 766.description: Solid-state light sources converting electricity directly into light and their societal impacts. Includes principles, fabrication, and applications of solid-state lamps and lighting systems.
ELCT 766.subject: ELCT
ELCT 766.title: Solid-State Lighting

ELCT 772.description: Advanced topics in power electronics to include rectifiers, inverters, resonant and soft switching converters, power converter system stability issues.
ELCT 772.subject: ELCT
ELCT 772.title: Advanced Power Electronics

ELCT 773.description: Magnetics design for power electronic converters with a focus on kHz and kW designs including inductors and transformers with integrated thermal designs.
ELCT 773.subject: ELCT
ELCT 773.title: Magnetics Design for Power Electronics

ELCT 774.description: Advanced semiconductor material characterization; Hall effect and mobility measurements, optical characterization, scanning probe microscopy, electron microscopy, X-Ray diffraction techniques; nanoscale characterization techniques.
ELCT 774.subject: ELCT
ELCT 774.title: Advanced Semiconductor Characterization

ELCT 782.description: The function and theory of operation of power semiconductor devices.
ELCT 782.subject: ELCT
ELCT 782.title: Power Semiconductor Devices

ELCT 797.description: Individual research to be arranged with the instructor.
ELCT 797.subject: ELCT
ELCT 797.title: Research

ELCT 837.description: The analysis and synthesis of linear, nonlinear, and discrete control systems employing the state space approach.
ELCT 837.subject: ELCT
ELCT 837.title: Modern Control Theory

ELCT 838.description: Optimal filtering, prediction, and smoothing in the presence of uncertainty.
ELCT 838.subject: ELCT
ELCT 838.title: Optimal Control and Estimation

ELCT 839.description: Theory and rigorous mathematical foundation for synthesis and analysis of robust adaptive controls for systems with uncertain dynamics. Lyapunov stability theory, robust control analysis, methods for model reference adaptive control with emphasis on L1 adaptive control.
ELCT 839.subject: ELCT
ELCT 839.title: Robust Adaptive Control

ELCT 861.description: Special topics of current interest in Communications and Electromagnetics. Content varies by semester and will be identified by a specific subtitle.
ELCT 861.subject: ELCT
ELCT 861.title: Special Topics in Communications and Electromagnetics

ELCT 862.description: Radiation mechanism and fundamental parameters. Dipoles, monopoles, and loop antennas. Antenna arrays. Microstrip, helical, biconical, sleeve, spiral, and log-periodic dipole antennas. Horn and reflector antennas. Antenna measurement and modeling.
ELCT 862.subject: ELCT
ELCT 862.title: Antennas and Radiation

ELCT 863.description: Electric and magnetic field integral equations, the moment method (MM). Finite element method (FEM), discretization and interpolation, system of equations. Finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, stability, dispersion, incident wave, absorbing boundary conditions (ABCs).
ELCT 863.subject: ELCT
ELCT 863.title: Computational Electromagnetics

ELCT 864.description: Microwave semiconductor diodes and transistors; active and passive microwave circuits.
ELCT 864.subject: ELCT
ELCT 864.title: Microwave Devices and Circuits

ELCT 870.description: Use and development of computer software applications for modeling and simulation of energy systems.
ELCT 870.subject: ELCT
ELCT 870.title: Computing Methods for System Simulation

ELCT 874.description: Principles and technology involved in the growth of both bulk and thin films of advanced semiconductor materials used in the fabrication of next generation electronic devices. Topics include principles of crystal growth, types of defects, and defect generation mechanisms.
ELCT 874.subject: ELCT
ELCT 874.title: Advanced Semiconductor Materials

ELCT 883.description: Power system transient and dynamic stability analysis. Power system control, including excitation systems, automatic generation control and boiler-turbine-generator models.
ELCT 883.subject: ELCT
ELCT 883.title: Power Systems Stability and Control

ELCT 897.description: Approved plan of study must be filed.
ELCT 897.subject: ELCT
ELCT 897.title: Directed Individual Study
